inscriptions.inscription_translation: The mount of Maharana Shri Raj (?) Singh
inscriptions.inscription_remark: This indistinct inscription appears to have been added later. Raj Singh reigned from 1754 to 1761 and was the immediate predecessor of the king who commissioned the portraits of elephants in the Udaipur royal stable.

In the Udaipur "jotdān" (royal painting storeroom), inventory numbers were written in red by clerks on the versos of each painting in the collection. The upper number is the class number; the lower number its serial number. The number 13 was used to classify pictures of elephants. See Andrew Topsfield, "Royal Paintings Inventory at Udaipur," in Indian Art & Connoisseurship, edited by John Guy, 1995, pp. 188 ff.

did_you_know: The name Ramkali is a popular nickname for young girls in some parts of northern India.
description: The mahout (elephant driver), directs the confident female elephant at a brisk trot, with bells swinging in response to her movements. This painting belongs to a series depicting the elephants in the royal stables at Udaipur, each one named in the upper margin. Elephants have been a potent emblem for royalty in India for more than three thousand years.
